correctness.rationale: Fourier reduction is exact on each odd cycle. The endpoint min-max lower bound is proved globally by restricting both feasible weights to at least \(1/b\) and applying \((B-x)(B-y)\ge0\); uniqueness follows at endpoint balancing. The achieved quadratic has only one possible negative trough, bounded by \(1/24\) against an endpoint modulus of at least \(1/6\). The repeated-step comparator and strict improvement are exact algebra. The delivered standard-library checker passed 22455 finite assertions, which supplement rather than replace the analytic all-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: Two independently stochastic rounds are natural in gossip and consensus; the theorem solves a constrained yet nontrivial minimax question over every odd cycle. The optimum is attained at the zero-holding boundary, is unique up to time reversal, and strictly improves on the best stationary walk (five-vertex factor \(1/6\) versus \(1/5\)). Its exact gain and \(n^{-6}\) limit quantify the benefit and limitation of admissible time variation without claiming Chebyshev-order acceleration.
